Bitcoin Billionaire is an idle/clicker hybrid for iOS and Android developed by Fizzpow and distributed by Noodlecake Studios. This review is for the iPad Air 2 version of the game.

Tap the 8 bit style screen to collect bitcoins which you use to buy investments that further generate bitcoins as well as upgrade the power of your taps, and to get new stuff for your room (or a whole new room). Collect gems from the random Amazon drone deliveries to enable off-screen production of bitcoins from your investments, as well as pick up a few other upgrades. There are also random events that can give you boosts, and challenges you can complete for bonuses.

I am going to say this now. I hate this game, but my reasons why are not immediately obvious. Stick with me here, and I will do my best to explain. First, the game uses the familiar to draw you in. Memes, pop culture jokes, and references to internet humor are used to great effect to make the player feel comfortable and welcome. You start to progress, and you see how simple it is to collect the gems, which are the in-game currency. There's a limit of 25 per day, but that isn't awful. It is an idle game, after all. Then you get a random event! Something good happens, woo! And you can spend a few of those gems or watch an ad to make it much, much better. Awesome!

It continues. You run out of those gems. Oh well, more tomorrow. But hark! A random event! Oh crap, no income for 5 minutes. But! You can shrug it off if you watch this one ad. Okay, cool. One ad later, and we're back in busines. Another random event! ...Lose one of your most expensive investments. That's big, I can't take that loss. I'll just watch an ad... "No ads available at this time". Now I have two choices. Take the hit and lose something that took me a day to work up to, or buy the gems. I took the third choice, and stopped playing.

Listen, I appreciate the need for a game to monetize, especially when the game is your primary income. But if you're going to use gambler hooks and negative reinforcement to get me to buy, I'm done. The worst part is that the game wasn't terrible. I even found myself enjoying it for a while. But the sheer volume of things they do to get you to spend money is borderline abusive, and I refuse to take part. Enjoy at your own discretion.
